sanskrit: ya eṣa gandharvapate pūrveṣāṃ naḥ purohitaḥ āsīd etan mamācakṣva ka eṣa bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: O lord of the Gandharvas, who was this one who served as the family priest of our ancestors? Tell me of him — who indeed is this venerable sage?

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca tapasā nirjitau śaśvad ajeyāv amarair api kāmakrodhāv ubhau yasya caraṇau saṃvavāhatuḥ
english: The Gandharva said: He whose two feet were forever massaged by desire and anger — both of them conquered by his austerity, those two who are ever unconquerable even by the immortals —

sanskrit: yas tu nocchedanaṃ cakre kuśikānām udāradhīḥ viśvāmitrāparādhena dhārayan manyum uttamam
english: who, though of noble spirit, did not bring about the destruction of the Kuśikas despite Viśvāmitra's offense, even while bearing the greatest wrath within —

sanskrit: putravyasanasaṃtaptaḥ śaktimān api yaḥ prabhuḥ viśvāmitravināśāya na mene karma dāruṇam
english: who, though powerful and lordly and tormented by the calamity of his sons, did not choose the terrible deed of destroying Viśvāmitra —

sanskrit: mṛtāṃś ca punar āhartuṃ yaḥ sa putrān yamakṣayāt kṛtāntaṃ nāticakrāma velām iva mahodadhiḥ
english: who, even to bring back his dead sons from Yama's realm, did not transgress fate, just as the great ocean does not transgress its shore —

sanskrit: yaṃ prāpya vijitātmānaṃ mahātmānaṃ narādhipāḥ ikṣvākavo mahīpālā lebhire pṛthivīm imām
english: having obtained whom — that self-conquered, great-souled one — the Ikṣvāku kings, those guardians of the earth, won this world —

sanskrit: purohitavaraṃ prāpya vasiṣṭham ṛṣisattamam ījire kratubhiś cāpi nṛpās te kurunandana
english: having obtained Vasiṣṭha, the best of household priests, the foremost of sages, those kings performed sacrifices, O joy of the Kurus —

sanskrit: sa hi tān yājayām āsa sarvān nṛpatisattamān brahmarṣiḥ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha bṛhaspatir ivāmarān
english: for that brahmarshi presided over the sacrifices of all those foremost kings, O best of the Pāṇḍavas, just as Bṛhaspati does for the immortals —

sanskrit: tasmād dharmapradhānātmā vedadharmavid īpsitaḥ brāhmaṇo guṇavān kaś cit purodhāḥ pravimṛśyatām
english: therefore a brahmin who is foremost in righteousness, who knows the dharma of the Vedas, who is sought-after and endowed with virtues — some such one should be carefully chosen as your priest.

sanskrit: kṣatriyeṇa hi jātena pṛthivīṃ jetum icchatā pūrvaṃ purohitaḥ kāryaḥ pārtha rājyābhivṛddhaye
english: For a man born as a kshatriya who desires to conquer the earth must first appoint a household priest, O Pārtha, for the increase of his kingdom.

sanskrit: mahīṃ jigīṣatā rājñā brahma kāryaṃ puraḥsaram tasmāt purohitaḥ kaś cid guṇavān astu vo dvijaḥ
english: A king who desires to conquer the earth must place a brahmin at the fore; therefore let some virtuous twice-born one be your household priest.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kiṃnimittam abhūd vairaṃ viśvāmitravasiṣṭhayoḥ vasator āśrame puṇye śaṃsa naḥ sarvam eva tat
english: Arjuna said: What was the cause of the enmity between Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha as they dwelt in their holy hermitage? Tell us all of that fully.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca idaṃ vāsiṣṭham ākhyānaṃ purāṇaṃ paricakṣate pārtha sarveṣu lokeṣu yathāvat tan nibodha me
english: The Gandharva said: This ancient tale of Vasiṣṭha is told throughout all the worlds, O Pārtha. Learn it fully from me.

sanskrit: kanyakubje mahān āsīt pārthivo bharatarṣabha gādhīti viśruto loke satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ
english: In Kanyakubja there was a great king, O bull among Bhāratas, known in the world as Gādhi — devoted to truth and righteousness.

sanskrit: tasya dharmātmanaḥ putraḥ samṛddhabalavāhanaḥ viśvāmitra iti khyāto babhūva ripumardanaḥ
english: This righteous king's son, possessed of abundant forces and mounts, became known as Viśvāmitra, the crusher of foes.

sanskrit: sa cacāra sahāmātyo mṛgayāṃ gahane vane mṛgān vidhyan varāhāṃś ca ramyeṣu marudhanvasu
english: He roamed the hunt with his ministers through dense forest, piercing deer and boars in the pleasant sandy tracts.

sanskrit: vyāyāmakarśitaḥ so 'tha mṛgalipsuḥ pipāsitaḥ ājagāma naraśreṣṭha vasiṣṭhasyāśramaṃ prati
english: Worn thin by exertion, eager for game and overcome with thirst, he came, O foremost of men, toward the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: tam āgatam abhiprekṣya vasiṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhabhāg ṛṣiḥ viśvāmitraṃ naraśreṣṭhaṃ pratijagrāha pūjayā
english: Seeing him arrive, Vasiṣṭha the sage, foremost in good fortune, received Viśvāmitra, that foremost of men, with full honor.

sanskrit: pādyārghyācamanīyena svāgatena ca bhārata tathaiva pratijagrāha vanyena haviṣā tathā
english: With water for the feet, the guest-offering, water for sipping, and a warm welcome, O Bhārata, he received him likewise with forest oblations.

sanskrit: tasyātha kāmadhug dhenur vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ uktā kāmān prayaccheti sā kāmān duduhe tataḥ
english: Then the wish-granting cow of great-souled Vasiṣṭha, told to yield all desires, duly milked them forth.

sanskrit: grāmyāraṇyā oṣadhīś ca duduhe paya eva ca ṣaḍrasaṃ cāmṛtarasaṃ rasāyanam anuttamam
english: She milked herbs both domestic and wild, and milk itself, and the six tastes, and the nectar-like juice, the unsurpassed elixir of life.

sanskrit: bhojanīyāni peyāni bhakṣyāṇi vividhāni ca lehyāny amṛtakalpāni coṣyāṇi ca tathārjuna
english: Foods to be eaten, liquids to be drunk, various delicacies to be chewed, lickable things akin to ambrosia, and things to be sucked — all of these, O Arjuna.

sanskrit: taiḥ kāmaiḥ sarvasaṃpūrṇaiḥ pūjitaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ sāmātyaḥ sabalaś caiva tutoṣa sa bhṛśaṃ nṛpaḥ
english: Honored with all those desires fully provided, that lord of the earth together with his ministers and army was greatly pleased, that king.

sanskrit: ṣaḍāyatāṃ supārśvoruṃ tripṛthuṃ pañca saṃvṛtām maṇḍūkanetrāṃ svākārāṃ pīnodhasam aninditām
english: With six elongated parts, fine flanks and thighs, three broad parts and five contracted ones, frog-like eyes, perfect form, and full udder — blameless —

sanskrit: suvāladhiṃ śaṅkukarṇāṃ cāruśṛṅgāṃ manoramām puṣṭāyataśirogrīvāṃ vismitaḥ so 'bhivīkṣya tām
english: with a handsome tail, spike-shaped ears, beautiful horns, and a lovely form, with well-nourished, elongated head and neck — gazing at her in wonder —

sanskrit: abhinandati tāṃ nandīṃ vasiṣṭhasya payasvinīm abravīc ca bhṛśaṃ tuṣṭo viśvāmitro muniṃ tadā
english: delighted by Nandini, Vasiṣṭha's milk-cow, Viśvāmitra, greatly pleased, spoke to the sage:

sanskrit: arbudena gavāṃ brahman mama rājyena vā punaḥ nandinīṃ saṃprayacchasva bhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ mahāmune
english: "Give me Nandini, O brahmin, in exchange for ten million cows, or else for my kingdom — enjoy my kingdom, O great sage."

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca devatātithipitrartham ājyārthaṃ ca payasvinī adeyā nandinīyaṃ me rājyenāpi tavānagha
english: Vasiṣṭha said: For the sake of the gods, guests, and ancestors, and for clarified butter offerings, this milk-cow Nandini is not to be given away by me, even for your kingdom, O sinless one.

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca kṣatriyo 'haṃ bhavān vipras tapaḥsvādhyāyasādhanaḥ brāhmaṇeṣu kuto vīryaṃ praśānteṣu dhṛtātmasu
english: Viśvāmitra said: I am a kshatriya; you are a brahmin whose means are austerity and Vedic study. Where does valor reside in brahmins, who are tranquil and self-controlled?

sanskrit: arbudena gavāṃ yas tvaṃ na dadāsi mamepsitām svadharmaṃ na prahāsyāmi nayiṣye te balena gām
english: "Since you will not give me what I desire even for ten million cows, I will not abandon my own duty — I shall take your cow by force."

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca balasthaś cāsi rājā ca bāhuvīryaś ca kṣatriyaḥ yathecchasi tathā kṣipraṃ kuru tvaṃ mā vicāraya
english: Vasiṣṭha said: You stand in power; you are a king; you are a kshatriya of mighty arm. Do quickly as you wish — do not deliberate.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca evam uktas tadā pārtha viśvāmitro balād iva haṃsacandrapratīkāśāṃ nandinīṃ tāṃ jahāra gām
english: The Gandharva said: Thus addressed, O Pārtha, Viśvāmitra then seized by force that cow Nandini, who resembled a swan or the moon.

sanskrit: kaśādaṇḍapratihatā kālyamānā tatas tataḥ hambhāyamānā kalyāṇī vasiṣṭhasyātha nandinī
english: Struck by whips and staffs, driven this way and that, lowing aloud, that auspicious Nandini of Vasiṣṭha —

sanskrit: āgamyābhimukhī pārtha tasthau bhagavadunmukhī bhṛśaṃ ca tāḍyamānāpi na jagāmāśramāt tataḥ
english: turned back and stood facing him, O Pārtha, her face turned toward her lord; though beaten hard, she did not leave the hermitage.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca śṛṇomi te ravaṃ bhadre vinadantyāḥ punaḥ punaḥ balād dhriyasi me nandi kṣamāvān brāhmaṇo hy aham
english: Vasiṣṭha said: I hear your cry, dear one, as you call out again and again. You are being carried off by force, O Nandī — but I am a brahmin, and forbearance is my nature.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca sā tu teṣāṃ balān nandī balānāṃ bharatarṣabha viśvāmitrabhayodvignā vasiṣṭhaṃ samupāgamat
english: The Gandharva said: But Nandini, overpowered by the force of those forces, O bull among Bhāratas, terrified of Viśvāmitra, came to Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: gaur uvāca pāṣāṇadaṇḍābhihatāṃ krandantīṃ mām anāthavat viśvāmitrabalair ghorair bhagavan kim upekṣase
english: The cow said: O lord, why do you ignore me as though I have no protector — me, who am being beaten with stones and staffs, crying out, beset by the terrible forces of Viśvāmitra?

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca evaṃ tasyāṃ tadā partha dharṣitāyāṃ mahāmuniḥ na cukṣubhe na dhairyāc ca vicacāla dhṛtavrataḥ
english: The Gandharva said: Even as she was thus afflicted, O Pārtha, the great sage did not agitate, nor did he waver from his composure, firm in his vow.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca kṣatriyāṇāṃ balaṃ tejo brāhmaṇānāṃ kṣamā balam kṣamā māṃ bhajate tasmād gamyatāṃ yadi rocate
english: Vasiṣṭha said: The strength of kshatriyas is their energy; the strength of brahmins is forbearance. Forbearance attends me — so go, if you please.

sanskrit: gaur uvāca kiṃ nu tyaktāsmi bhagavan yad evaṃ māṃ prabhāṣase atyaktāhaṃ tvayā brahman na śakyā nayituṃ balāt
english: The cow said: Have I been abandoned by you, lord, that you speak to me thus? I have not truly been abandoned by you, O brahmin — I cannot be taken away by force.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca na tvāṃ tyajāmi kalyāṇi sthīyatāṃ yadi śakyate dṛḍhena dāmnā baddhvaiṣa vatsas te hriyate balāt
english: Vasiṣṭha said: I do not abandon you, O auspicious one. Stay, if you are able. They have bound your calf with strong rope and are carrying it off by force.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca sthīyatām iti tac chrutvā vasiṣṭhasya payasvinī ūrdhvāñcitaśirogrīvā prababhau ghoradarśanā
english: The Gandharva said: Hearing those words "Stay!" from Vasiṣṭha, his milk-cow raised her head and neck upward and blazed forth, terrible to behold.

sanskrit: krodharaktekṣaṇā sā gaur hambhāravaghanasvanā viśvāmitrasya tat sainyaṃ vyadrāvayata sarvaśaḥ
english: That cow, with eyes red with fury and a dense thunderous bellow, scattered Viśvāmitra's entire army in every direction.

sanskrit: kaśāgradaṇḍābhihatā kālyamānā tatas tataḥ krodhadīptekṣaṇā krodhaṃ bhūya eva samādadhe
english: Struck by the tips of whips and staffs, driven here and there, her eyes blazing with wrath, she gathered yet more wrath within her.

sanskrit: āditya iva madhyāhne krodhadīptavapur babhau aṅgāravarṣaṃ muñcantī muhur vāladhito mahat
english: She blazed, her body lit with fury like the midday sun, repeatedly raining down a great shower of embers from her tail.

sanskrit: asṛjat pahlavān pucchāc chakṛtaḥ śabarāñ śakān mūtrataś cāsṛjac cāpi yavanān krodhamūrcchitā
english: From her tail she created the Pahlavas; from her dung she created Śabaras and Śakas; maddened with rage, from her urine she created the Yavanas.

sanskrit: puṇḍrān kirātān dramiḍān siṃhalān barbarāṃs tathā tathaiva daradān mlecchān phenataḥ sā sasarja ha
english: From her foam she created Puṇḍras, Kirātas, Dravidians, Sinhalese, Barbaras, and likewise Daradas and other barbarians.

sanskrit: tair visṛṣṭair mahat sainyaṃ nānāmlecchagaṇais tadā nānāvaraṇasaṃchannair nānāyudhadharais tathā avākīryata saṃrabdhair viśvāmitrasya paśyataḥ
english: By those created hosts, bands of various barbarians clad in varied armor and bearing varied weapons, the great army of Viśvāmitra was overwhelmed as he looked on.

sanskrit: ekaikaś ca tadā yodhaḥ pañcabhiḥ saptabhir vṛtaḥ astravarṣeṇa mahatā kālyamānaṃ balaṃ tataḥ prabhagnaṃ sarvatas trastaṃ viśvāmitrasya paśyataḥ
english: Each warrior was surrounded by five or seven, and the army of Viśvāmitra, driven by a great rain of weapons, was shattered on all sides, terrified, as he watched.

sanskrit: na ca prāṇair viyujyanta ke cit te sainikās tadā viśvāmitrasya saṃkruddhair vāsiṣṭhair bharatarṣabha
english: Yet none of those soldiers of Viśvāmitra were separated from their lives by the enraged forces of Vasiṣṭha, O bull among Bhāratas.

sanskrit: viśvāmitrasya sainyaṃ tu kālyamānaṃ triyojanam krośamānaṃ bhayodvignaṃ trātāraṃ nādhyagacchata
english: The army of Viśvāmitra, driven back three yojanas, crying out, seized with fear, found no protector.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tan mahad āścaryaṃ brahmatejobhavaṃ tadā viśvāmitraḥ kṣatrabhāvān nirviṇṇo vākyam abravīt
english: Seeing that great wonder born of brahmanic splendor, Viśvāmitra, disillusioned with the nature of the kshatriya, spoke these words:

sanskrit: dhig balaṃ kṣatriyabalaṃ brahmatejobalaṃ balam balābalaṃ viniścitya tapa eva paraṃ balam
english: "Shame on the strength of the kshatriya! The strength of brahmic splendor is true strength. Having weighed strength against strength, I conclude that austerity alone is supreme strength."

sanskrit: sa rājyaṃ sphītam utsṛjya tāṃ ca dīptāṃ nṛpaśriyam bhogāṃś ca pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā tapasy eva mano dadhe
english: Renouncing his flourishing kingdom, that blazing royal glory, and leaving all pleasures behind, he turned his mind solely to austerity.

sanskrit: sa gatvā tapasā siddhiṃ lokān viṣṭabhya tejasā tatāpa sarvān dīptaujā brāhmaṇatvam avāpa ca apibac ca sutaṃ somam indreṇa saha kauśikaḥ
english: Having attained perfection through austerity, pervading the worlds with his splendor, blazing in energy he scorched all beings and won brahminhood; and that Kauśika drank the soma juice together with Indra.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca kalmāṣapāda ity asmiṃl loke rājā babhūva ha ikṣvākuvaṃśajaḥ pārtha tejasāsadṛśo bhuvi
english: The Gandharva said: There was a king known as Kalmāṣapāda in this world, O Pārtha — born of the Ikṣvāku lineage, unmatched on earth in his splendor.

sanskrit: sa kadā cid vanaṃ rājā mṛgayāṃ niryayau purāt mṛgān vidhyan varāhāṃś ca cacāra ripumardanaḥ
english: Once that king, crusher of enemies, went out from his city into the forest for the hunt, piercing deer and boars as he roamed.

sanskrit: sa tu rājā mahātmānaṃ vāsiṣṭham ṛṣisattamam tṛṣārtaś ca kṣudhārtaś ca ekāyanagataḥ pathi
english: That king, afflicted by thirst and hunger, was travelling alone on a narrow path when he encountered great-souled Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of sages.

sanskrit: apaśyad ajitaḥ saṃkhye muniṃ pratimukhāgatam śaktiṃ nāma mahābhāgaṃ vasiṭhakulanandanam jyeṣṭhaṃ putraśatāt putraṃ vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ
english: That unconquered-in-battle king saw coming toward him a sage named Shakti — highly blessed, the delight of Vasiṣṭha's line, the eldest among the hundred sons of great-souled Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: apagaccha patho 'smākam ity evaṃ pārthivo 'bravīt tathā ṛṣir uvācainaṃ sāntvayañ ślakṣṇayā girā
english: "Leave our path!" — thus spoke the king. And the sage spoke back to him, calming him with gentle words.

sanskrit: ṛṣis tu nāpacakrāma tasmin dharmapathe sthitaḥ nāpi rājā muner mānāt krodhāc cāpi jagāma ha
english: But the sage did not step aside, standing firm on that path of dharma; nor did the king move away, out of pride toward the sage and also out of anger.

sanskrit: amuñcantaṃ tu panthānaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ nṛpasattamaḥ jaghāna kaśayā mohāt tadā rākṣasavan munim
english: That best of kings, in delusion, then struck with a whip the sage who would not yield the path — struck him as though he were a demon.

sanskrit: kaśāprahārābhihatas tataḥ sa munisattamaḥ taṃ śaśāpa nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ vāsiṣṭhaḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ
english: Struck by the blow of the whip, that foremost of sages, Vasiṣṭha's son, overcome with rage, cursed that best of kings:

sanskrit: haṃsi rākṣasavad yasmād rājāpasada tāpasam tasmāt tvam adya prabhṛti puruṣādo bhaviṣyasi
english: "Because you strike an ascetic like a demon, O lowest of kings, from this day forward you shall become a man-eater."

sanskrit: manuṣyapiśite saktaś cariṣyasi mahīm imām gaccha rājādhamety uktaḥ śaktinā vīryaśaktinā
english: "Addicted to human flesh, you shall roam this earth" — thus spoken to by Shakti, that Shakti of mighty power, "Go, O vilest of kings!"

sanskrit: tato yājyanimittaṃ tu viśvāmitravasiṣṭhayoḥ vairam āsīt tadā taṃ tu viśvāmitro 'nvapadyata
english: Now the enmity between Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha had arisen over the matter of whose sacrificial client the king was — and Viśvāmitra followed that king.

sanskrit: tayor vivadator evaṃ samīpam upacakrame ṛṣir ugratapāḥ pārtha viśvāmitraḥ pratāpavān
english: As these two were thus in conflict, the sage Viśvāmitra of fierce austerity, O Pārtha, the illustrious one, drew near.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bubudhe paścāt tam ṛṣiṃ nṛpasattamaḥ ṛṣeḥ putraṃ vasiṣṭhasya vasiṣṭham iva tejasā
english: Then that best of kings afterward recognized the sage — the son of the sage Vasiṣṭha, equal to Vasiṣṭha himself in splendor.

sanskrit: antardhāya tadātmānaṃ viśvāmitro 'pi bhārata tāv ubhāv upacakrāma cikīrṣann ātmanaḥ priyam
english: Viśvāmitra too, O Bhārata, concealing himself, approached both of them, wishing to do what was pleasing to himself.

sanskrit: sa tu śaptas tadā tena śaktinā vai nṛpottamaḥ jagāma śaraṇaṃ śaktiṃ prasādayitum arhayan
english: The best of kings, thus cursed by Shakti, went to seek refuge with Shakti, worthy of placating him.

sanskrit: tasya bhāvaṃ viditvā sa nṛpateḥ kurunandana viśvāmitras tato rakṣa ādideśa nṛpaṃ prati
english: Knowing the king's intention, O joy of the Kurus, Viśvāmitra then directed a demon against the king.

sanskrit: sa śāpāt tasya viprarṣer viśvāmitrasya cājñayā rākṣasaḥ kiṃkaro nāma viveśa nṛpatiṃ tadā
english: By the curse of that brahmin-sage and by the command of Viśvāmitra, a demon named Kinkara then entered into the king.

sanskrit: rakṣasā tu gṛhītaṃ taṃ viditvā sa munis tadā viśvāmitro 'py apakrāmat tasmād deśād ariṃdama
english: Knowing that the king had been seized by the demon, that sage Viśvāmitra then withdrew from that place, O crusher of enemies.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa nṛpatir vidvān rakṣann ātmānam ātmanā balavat pīḍyamāno 'pi rakṣasāntargatena ha
english: Then that wise king, guarding himself by his own self, was powerfully tormented even so by the demon that had entered within him.

sanskrit: dadarśa taṃ dvijaḥ kaś cid rājānaṃ prasthitaṃ punaḥ yayāce kṣudhitaś cainaṃ samāṃsaṃ bhojanaṃ tadā
english: A certain brahmin saw that king setting out again, and, being hungry, begged from him food along with meat.

sanskrit: tam uvācātha rājarṣir dvijaṃ mitrasahas tadā āssva brahmaṃs tvam atraiva muhūrtam iti sāntvayan
english: The royal sage Mitrasaha then spoke to that brahmin, placating him: "Stay here for just a moment, O brahmin."

sanskrit: nivṛttaḥ pratidāsyāmi bhojanaṃ te yathepsitam ity uktvā prayayau rājā tasthau ca dvijasattamaḥ
english: "When I return I shall give you food as you desire" — so saying, the king departed, and that best of brahmins waited.

sanskrit: antargataṃ tu tad rājñas tadā brāhmaṇabhāṣitam so 'ntaḥpuraṃ praviśyātha saṃviveśa narādhipaḥ
english: The brahmin's words had meanwhile entered within the king's mind; and that lord of men entered his inner apartments and retired.

sanskrit: tato 'rdharātra utthāya sūdam ānāyya satvaram uvāca rājā saṃsmṛtya brāhmaṇasya pratiśrutam
english: Then at midnight the king arose, quickly summoned the cook, and spoke, remembering what he had promised the brahmin:

sanskrit: gacchāmuṣminn asau deśe brāhmaṇo māṃ pratīkṣate annārthī tvaṃ tam annena samāṃsenopapādaya
english: "Go — in that place a brahmin waits for me, seeking food. You must supply him with food together with meat."
